filename: Inter-Comparison of Deep Learning Models for Flood Forecasting in Ethiopia’s Upper Awash Basin.pdf
title: Inter-Comparison of Deep Learning Models for Flood Forecasting in Ethiopia’s Upper Awash Basin
testbed_rationale: Focuses on catchment-scale daily streamflow forecasting with empirical time series, not an atmospheric/oceanic subgrid parameterization or process emulation testbed.
pain_points: Underestimation of peak-flow magnitudes across all deep learning architectures due to MSE loss prioritizing average conditions over rare extremes
Generalization gap between validation and test datasets due to climate/interannual variability and unseen extremes
Reduced performance during dry season / low-flow conditions where baseflow dynamics dominate over direct rainfall response
Absence of uncertainty quantification limiting operational early-warning deployment
extraction_notes: Author Addisu G. Semie acknowledges funding from the NSF LEAP STC (Award #2019625). Baseline models include long-term daily climatology and a calibrated conceptual HBV rainfall-runoff model.
